page: UpCloud STARTER-1xCPU-4GB is an entry-level virtual server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features a single shared vCPU mapped to an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is provisioned with 4.0 GB of system memory and includes 30 GB of local SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU allocation is shared, meaning compute resources are multiplexed across multiple tenants, which represents a common tradeoff for budget-oriented tiers.

Benchmark data highlights a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Due to its single-thread configuration, the instance achieves top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng and single-threaded compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core and parallelized workloads perform poorly, with Geekbench multi-core and software compilation benchmarks scoring in the bottom 10% of tested systems. Memory performance is also constrained, with PassMark memory scores in the bottom 10% and uncached read bandwidth limited to 36.02 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a highly accessible entry point for workloads that do not require continuous, high-density parallel processing. The combination of 4.0 GB of RAM with a single high-performing single-thread core makes it suitable for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and low-traffic static web serving. It is less suitable for database operations, multi-threaded compilation, or memory-intensive tasks, where the shared CPU allocation and low memory bandwidth present clear performance bottlenecks.
